title: Panorra API Go New Project Report

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 05/08/26

✅ Implementation: Upload Avatar V2

Summary

Added a dedicated V2 avatar endpoint for the logged-in user.

API Contract

Route

PUT /v2/users/me/avatar
Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

The authenticated token determines the user. The endpoint does not accept a user ID.

Payload

Field Type Required Rules
avatar File Yes JPG, JPEG, or PNG; maximum 800 KB; maximum 400 x 400 pixels
ec Text No Set to true to return encrypted cry and login timestamp ls

Example using cURL:

curl --request PUT "{{base_url}}/v2/users/me/avatar" \
  --header "Authorization: <JWT token>" \
  --form "avatar=@/path/to/avatar.png" \
  --form "ec=true"

Success Response

Without ec=true, status 200 OK:

Status: 200 OK

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "avatar": "<raw value generated by GenerateImageURL>",
    "messages": "Success upload avatar",
    "valid": true
  }
}

With ec=true, status 200 OK:

{
  "cry": "<AES-encrypted base64 response>",
  "ls": 1785916800
}

cry encrypts this response envelope using the same KeyEncrypt and EncryptResult flow as AddPostCompleteV1:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "avatar": "<raw value generated by GenerateImageURL>",
    "messages": "Success upload avatar",
    "valid": true
  }
}

Validation Responses

Missing avatar, status 422 Unprocessable Entity:

{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unprocessable Entity",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Required Param Avatar",
      "input": "avatar"
    }
  }
}

File larger than 800 KB, status 413 Request Entity Too Large:

{
  "statusCode": 413,
  "data": {
    "status": "Request Entity Too Large",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Image file size too large, max 800kb",
      "input": "avatar"
    }
  }
}

Invalid filename extension, status 422 Unprocessable Entity:

{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unprocessable Entity",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "File Extension not valid, must be jpg, jpeg, png",
      "input": "avatar"
    }
  }
}

Image dimensions exceed 400 x 400 pixels, status 422 Unprocessable Entity:

{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unprocessable Entity",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Image dimension too large, max 400px",
      "input": "avatar"
    }
  }
}

Invalid detected MIME type, status 400 Bad Request:

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Request",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Extension panorama not valid",
      "input": "extension available is jpg, jpeg, png, JPG, JPEG, PNG"
    }
  }
}

Unauthorized role, status 401 Unauthorized:

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unauthorized",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Unauthorized"
    }
  }
}

Missing or invalid JWT is rejected earlier by auth middleware with 401 Unauthorized.

User not found, status 409 Conflict:

{
  "statusCode": 409,
  "data": {
    "status": "Conflict",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "User not found"
    }
  }
}

Storage, signing, database, or cleanup failures return 500 Internal Server Error using the common ErrorResponse envelope.

Processing Flow

  1. Validate authenticated role and load id, existing avatar, and existing path.
  2. Validate multipart file size, filename extension, detected MIME type, and dimensions.
  3. Save the new image locally, create the MinIO bucket when needed, then upload it.
  4. Generate the raw imgproxy value using GenerateImageURL.
  5. Update users.avatar, users.path, and users.updated_at.
  6. Delete the previous MinIO object and local file using the values loaded before the update.
  7. Refresh Redis user details and sync Maps Panorra when PREFIX=live.
  8. When multipart field ec=true, encrypt the success envelope and return cry plus ls; otherwise return the plain success payload.

Changes Applied

  • src/Routes/V1/Routes.go
    • Registered the global /v2 route group.
  • src/Routes/V2/UsersRoutes.go
    • Registered PUT /v2/users/me/avatar.
  • src/Controllers/V2/UsersController.go
    • Added the V2 upload controller.
  • src/Action/V2/Users/UploadAvatar.go
    • Validates role, file size, extension, MIME type, and dimensions.
    • Uploads the new file to local storage and MinIO.
    • Generates the imgproxy value and updates users.avatar and users.path.
    • Deletes the old MinIO/local file using the user data loaded before update.
    • Refreshes Redis and triggers Maps Panorra sync on live.
    • Returns the common statusCode and data envelope for plain responses.
    • Returns encrypted cry and ls when multipart field ec=true.
  • src/Routes/V2/UsersRoutes_test.go
    • Verifies route registration.
  • api-collection/Panorra API Post/User/Upload Avatar V2.yml
    • Added multipart API request and success example.

Verification

go test ./src/Routes/V2 -run TestRegisterUsersRoutesRegistersUploadAvatar -count=1
go test ./... -count=1
git diff --check

Results:

  • V2 route test passed.
  • Full Go test suite passed.
  • Diff whitespace check passed.

Background

Avatar upload was coupled to the legacy POST /users/edit-profile endpoint. V2 needs a dedicated authenticated endpoint without changing legacy behavior.

Objective

Add PUT /v2/users/me/avatar for the logged-in user and return the generated imgproxy value directly.

Scope

  • Add a global /v2 route group.
  • Add V2 route, controller, and action packages.
  • Accept multipart field avatar.
  • Preserve legacy avatar validation and upload flow.
  • Update users.avatar and users.path.
  • Remove the previous MinIO and local avatar after the DB update.
  • Refresh Redis and sync Maps Panorra on live.
  • Add API collection request.
  • Support encrypted response when multipart field ec=true.

Constraints

  • Do not modify EditProfile behavior.
  • Resolve the user only from authentication locals.
  • Maximum size: 800 KB.
  • Allowed formats: JPG, JPEG, PNG.
  • Maximum dimensions: 400 x 400 pixels.
  • Return the raw value produced by GenerateImageURL.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Authenticated user can upload an avatar through PUT /v2/users/me/avatar.
  • Plain success response uses the common statusCode and data envelope.
  • data contains valid, messages, and the raw imgproxy value in avatar.
  • With ec=true, response contains encrypted cry and login timestamp ls.
  • New avatar is stored before the old avatar is deleted.
  • V1 endpoint remains unchanged.
  • Full Go test suite passes.

RESULT 05/08/26

✅ Implementation: Upload Cover V2

Route

PUT /v2/users/me/cover
Authorization: <JWT token>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

Payload

Field Type Required Rules
cover File Yes JPG/JPEG/PNG/WebP, 10 KiB-8 MiB, width 1128-4000 px, height 191-4000 px
ec Text No true enables encrypted response 
curl --request PUT "{{base_url}}/v2/users/me/cover" \
  --header "Authorization: <JWT token>" \
  --form "cover=@/path/to/cover.webp" \
  --form "ec=true"

Responses

Plain 200 OK:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "cover": "<raw imgproxy value>",
    "messages": "Success upload cover",
    "valid": true
  }
}

Encrypted 200 OK with ec=true:

{
  "cry": "<encrypted success envelope>",
  "ls": 1785916800
}

Validation errors use the common envelope:

{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unprocessable Entity",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "<validation message>",
      "input": "cover"
    }
  }
}

Possible statuses: 401 invalid auth/role, 409 user missing, 413 over 8 MiB, 422 missing/invalid file, 500 storage/signing/database/cleanup failure.

Processing Flow

  1. Resolve authenticated user and retain old cover_path.
  2. Validate size, extension, MIME, width, and height. Ratio is omitted.
  3. Save locally and upload to MinIO using original format/MIME.
  4. Generate imgproxy value.
  5. Update cover_image, cover_path, and updated_at.
  6. Delete old MinIO/local cover.
  7. Refresh Redis.
  8. Return plain or encrypted response.

Files

  • migrations/20260805_add_user_cover.sql
  • src/Models/User.go
  • src/Routes/V2/UsersRoutes.go
  • src/Controllers/V2/UsersController.go
  • src/Action/V2/Users/UploadCover.go
  • src/Routes/V2/UsersRoutes_test.go
  • api-collection/Panorra API Post/User/Upload Cover V2.yml

Verification

go test ./src/Routes/V2 -run TestUserRoutesRegistersUploadCover -count=1
go test ./... -count=1
git diff --check

Objective

Add authenticated PUT /v2/users/me/cover without changing avatar or legacy profile behavior.

Scope

  • Add cover_image and cover_path to the user model.
  • Add SQL migration for both columns.
  • Add V2 route, controller, and action.
  • Add plain and encrypted response support.
  • Add route test and API collection.

Validation

  • Multipart field: cover.
  • Extensions: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .webp.
  • MIME types: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp.
  • Size: 10 KiB through 8 MiB.
  • Width: 1128 through 4000 pixels.
  • Height: 191 through 4000 pixels.
  • Ideal dimensions: 1584 x 396 pixels; informational only.
  • Aspect-ratio validation: disabled.

Acceptance Criteria

  • JWT-authenticated user updates only their own cover.
  • New cover uploads before the DB update and old-cover cleanup.
  • Plain response uses statusCode and data.
  • Multipart ec=true returns cry and ls.

RESULT 05/08/26

✅ Implementation: Auth Onboarding Completed

Response

Successful manual, Google, Apple, Apple after-register, Google/Apple registration, and OTP-check responses now contain:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "onboarding_completed": true
  }
}

Value may be false when onboarding is incomplete or no matching user_detail exists.

Updated Features

  1. Manual login: returns stored onboarding_completed.
  2. Google login: returns stored onboarding_completed.
  3. Apple login: returns stored onboarding_completed.
  4. Apple login after register: returns stored onboarding_completed supplied by the Apple registration lookup.
  5. Apple registration for a new user: returns onboarding_completed: false.
  6. Google registration for a new user: returns onboarding_completed: false.
  7. OTP verification: returns onboarding_completed: false after successful verification.

Manual registration is not changed. Its onboarding value is returned after successful OTP verification.

Processing

  1. Existing login query performs LEFT JOIN user_detail using user ID.
  2. Query selects onboarding_completed without an alias.
  3. Shared onboardingCompleted safely reads the boolean and defaults to false.
  4. Response builder adds it to data before plain or encrypted serialization.
  5. Apple registration lookup joins user_detail; LoginAppleAfterRegister reads onboarding state from the supplied user map.
  6. New Apple registration returns false directly because a new user has not completed onboarding.
  7. Google registration returns false directly. Manual registration remains unchanged.
  8. Successful OTP checks return false directly in plain and encrypted payloads.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Auth/Login.go
  • src/Action/V1/Auth/LoginGoogle.go
  • src/Action/V1/Auth/LoginApple.go
  • src/Action/V1/Register/RegisterApple.go
  • src/Action/V1/Register/RegisterGoogle.go
  • src/Action/V1/Users/CheckOtp.go

Excluded

  • Failed and unregistered login responses
  • SaveOnboarding behavior

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Auth -count=1
git diff --check

Full repository test may fail on Windows when executing Functions.test.exe with Access is denied; this is unrelated to these Auth changes.

Objective

Expose onboarding completion state across login, social registration, and OTP verification responses.

Scope

  • Join user_detail in manual login query.
  • Join user_detail in Google login query.
  • Join user_detail in Apple login query.
  • Add data.onboarding_completed to each successful login response.
  • Add data.onboarding_completed to LoginAppleAfterRegister success response.
  • Add data.onboarding_completed to new Apple registration success response.
  • Add data.onboarding_completed to Google registration success response.
  • Add data.onboarding_completed to successful OTP checks.
  • Keep failed login responses unchanged.

Acceptance Criteria

  • onboarding_completed is true when user_detail.onboarding_completed is true.
  • Missing or incomplete onboarding returns false.
  • Existing encrypted responses include the field inside the encrypted response payload.
  • No extra database query or new dependency is added.
  • Apple registration lookup joins user_detail, allowing its existing-user path to pass onboarding state into LoginAppleAfterRegister without another query.
  • New Apple registration returns false directly because onboarding has not started.
  • New Google registration returns false directly.
  • Manual registration response remains unchanged; onboarding status is returned after successful OTP verification.
  • Successful OTP checks return false directly.
